text:
Alex: quick idea — what if we separate allocator lease demarcation from queue-slice ownership?
Marta: curious, sketch it out. how do you see the separation helping latency jitter? :thinking:
Alex: current problem: frequent tiny evictions when leases and slice boundaries are coupled. every time lease rolls we requeue a bunch of inflight work.
Alex: decouple by making leases only track resource entitlement, and use a lightweight slice token to mark batch-affinity. slice tokens can be short-lived and garbage-collected without forcing full reenqueue.
Ryan: sounds promising. main tradeoff is starvation visibility — if slice tokens stick, tiny tenants might never get a slot.
Marta: agreed. we should bound slice lifetime and provide a preemptible flag. minute-level leases, sub-second slice tokens?
Alex: thinking: lease = 30s holo (renewable), slice token = 200-500ms affinity window. if a high-priority request arrives, token can be revoked and work fast-tracked.
Sam: how does this interact with KV cache pinning? we currently tie cache pins to batch membership. revoking slice tokens would need safe pin-release semantics.
Alex: good call. plan: add a pin reference count independent of slice token. slice release decrements a transient ref; cache holds until either TTL or explicit release.
Ryan: telemetry needs: per-slice lifetime histogram, slice revoke reasons, and per-tenant starvation counter. without those we won't know if token churn causes harm.
Marta: also expose "preemptible" vs "non-preemptible" slice metric, so SRE can tune headroom.
Alex: rough pseudo:
```
if (slice.age > SLICE_MAX || lease.revoked) {
  revoke_slice(slice)
  decrement_pin(ref)
  maybe_requeue(remaining)
}
```
Sam: what about fallback when allocator is under pressure? currently we fallback to smaller model variants; we should ensure slice revokes can trigger fast fallback paths.
Alex: yes — on revoke we can inline a quick policy: if tenant has fallback_model -> route immediately, else reenqueue with priority bump.
Ryan: imagine edge case: bursty tenant repeatedly gets small slices and always preempted. add backoff cooldown per-tenant so we avoid thrash.
Marta: +1. cooldown + token quanta (one tenant can hold at most N concurrent tokens).
Sam: ops question: will this require a control-plane schema change? storing slice tokens sounds like more ephemeral state we can keep in runtime memory, not CP.
Alex: prefer runtime-only ephemeral tokens, replicated via gossip/lease heartbeats. only leases remain in control plane. keeps CP stable.
Ryan: sounds good. we should prototype in a single-host experiment first, measure tail p50/p95 for small requests.
Marta: can we add a simple synthetic workload: many 8-token requests + one large tenant continuously. measure fairness and tail latency.
Alex: I'll spin up an experiment branch. plan: implement token revocation + pin refcounts + metrics. expect minimal CP change.
Sam: +1 for metrics and a rollback flag. also add a canary that forces tokens off for 10% of traffic.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: branch=alloc/slice-demarcation, env=canary, target=staging, run=terraform apply (in 3m) :rocket:
Ryan: nice. once we have numbers we can debate defaults (200ms vs 500ms).
Marta: thanks — this is a clean abstraction if we can get cache pins right.
Alex: will post PR and a short runbook for oncall in case of regressions.
Sam: 👍
Marta: :thumbsup:
